description: Hi everyone! I’m Raghad, a 10th-grade student from the UAE who loves space, physics, and tech. For the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer project, I want to build a fun, interactive experience that teaches kids what real astronaut training is like. I’m organized, easy to work with, and good at structuring ideas and solving problems so our team stays on track. I’m looking for creative and enthusiastic teammates who are interested in coding, graphic design.
summary: The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, web-based simulation designed to teach students space exploration dynamics, life support management, and lunar/Martian survival through gameplay. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the project addresses the complexity of space environmental hazards—such as lunar long dark nights, Martian dust storms, and solar radiation—by transforming them into an intuitive, strategic decision-making experience. Players manage core survival resources including Power, Oxygen, Shield integrity, and Science progress across mission days (Sols). By choosing daily operational strategies (Balanced Work, Fast Research, Shield Repair, or Oxygen/Power generation), astronauts must balance scientific discovery with survival. This project is important because it bridges authentic NASA space weather and exploration data (sourced from NASA DONKI, Artemis/LRO, and Mars 2020 Perseverance) with accessible STEM education. Running seamlessly in any browser without installation, it empowers 10th-grade students and junior learners to grasp complex systems engineering and space mission operations through hands-on gameplay.
details: How it Works: The application features a web interface built with HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, offering multi-screen navigation (Intro, Mission Dashboard, and Win/Loss End Screens). Players select either a Moon or Mars base and manage four critical resources: Power, Oxygen, Shield, and Science. Each "Sol" (day), players select an operational strategy that updates resource meters and checks win/loss conditions (reaching 100% Science wins the game). Tools & Languages: Developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (vanilla JS), hosted live on Netlify, with slide design created via Google Slides. Creativity & Impact: It transforms complex orbital mechanics and planetary survival constraints into a lightweight, highly accessible educational mini-game that runs in any browser with zero setup.
